decision: Use Neo4j as the knowledge graph backend instead of Postgres pgvector adjacency tables
reason: Neo4j provides native graph traversal, better performance for complex relationship queries, and cleaner visualization of traversal paths for the frontend

decision: Remove email ingestion and auto-project-creation entirely
reason: Manual project creation gives syndicate members explicit control over what data enters the system; auto-creation was passive and error-prone

decision: Make asset upload the primary input mechanism, supporting any file type (PDF, MP3, images, Excel, video)
reason: Investors have diverse materials (pitch decks, founder recordings, location photos, financial models); a single asset type would be limiting

decision: Stream knowledge graph traversal to the frontend in real-time via SSE
reason: Investors need to see exactly which information the system used to answer their question; this builds trust and transparency

decision: Use D3.js force-directed graph for frontend visualization with node pulse and edge draw animations
reason: D3 is battle-tested for interactive graphs; force-directed layout makes relationships intuitive; animations make traversal visible without overwhelming the viewer

decision: Support both text and voice input for investor conversations via Whisper STT
reason: Investors may prefer speaking (faster, more natural); voice input removes friction and captures tone/emphasis that text misses

decision: Capture investor views through conversation itself rather than form responses alone
reason: Conversational input is richer (questions reveal thesis, follow-ups show depth of thinking); forms are rigid and often incomplete

decision: Implement flow canvas using React Flow for cell/edge composition and D3.js force-directed graph for topic-scoped knowledge visualization
reason: React Flow is the standard for node-based UI composition; D3 handles the knowledge graph visualization within each cell's deep-dive. Separation of concerns keeps canvas logic clean.

decision: Extract InvestorView nodes from investor conversations as first-class Neo4j entities, embedded and linked to supporting/contradicting artifacts
reason: Investor views are the core analytical asset; making them queryable nodes in the graph allows cell synthesis to aggregate and compare views across investors transparently

decision: Persist flow canvas state (cells, edges, positions) in Postgres, not Neo4j
reason: Flow structure is admin-defined metadata, not knowledge; Postgres is simpler for CRUD and layout persistence. Neo4j stores the knowledge graph itself.

decision: Implement cell analysis as an async job (background worker) that builds InvestorView nodes and synthesizes output
reason: Cell analysis (extracting views, embedding, linking artifacts) is CPU-intensive; async prevents UI blocking and allows queuing/prioritization

decision: Ingest competitive intelligence as a standard asset type (competitive_intel) flowing through the existing pipeline
reason: Competitors participate in all existing traversal/conversation/analysis with zero special handling; no separate code paths needed; NER automatically links competitor entities to existing market concepts

decision: Trigger competitive scan automatically when project status transitions to open
reason: All assets are ready at that point; scan results are immediately available for investor conversations; re-run is a single button if needed

decision: Use Tavily API for competitive web search instead of building custom scraper
reason: Tavily handles deduplication, rate limiting, and result ranking; reduces operational burden; API key management is simpler than maintaining scraper infrastructure

decision: Build analysis flow canvas with React Flow and persist cell positions in Postgres (flow_cells, flow_edges tables)
reason: React Flow is battle-tested for node-based UIs; Postgres persistence is consistent with existing architecture; cell positions are UI state, not graph state

decision: Extract investor views as first-class Neo4j nodes (InvestorView) linked to entities and supporting/contradicting chunks
reason: Views participate in traversal as pink diamond nodes; investors see their own reasoning reflected back in the graph; enables consensus/rebuttal analysis without special-case code

decision: Scope cell-level GraphRAG traversal to a topic filter and include InvestorView nodes in results
reason: Keeps traversal focused on the cell's domain; investor views become first-class evidence; no separate analysis engine needed

decision: Use Serper API for competitive intelligence search instead of Tavily
reason: Serper provides better structured results (title, link, snippet) and is more cost-effective for bulk competitor discovery

decision: Ingest competitive intelligence as a standard asset through the existing pipeline rather than as a special data type
reason: Reusing the asset pipeline (chunking, embedding, Neo4j ingestion) avoids code duplication and ensures competitors are automatically cross-linked to pitch deck entities via NER

decision: Capture admin conversations within analysis flow cells as AdminConversationTurn nodes in Neo4j immediately after each turn

decision: Propagate upstream cell context to downstream cells in topological order via synthesis + conversation summary injection
reason: Multi-topic analysis requires each cell to build on prior findings; injecting upstream context into prompts enables reasoning chains without requiring manual copy-paste or separate context management

decision: Expose an /investments route on the frontend for syndicate members to view all projects they are included in

decision: Implement admin-driven cell deep-dive workflow with AdminConversationTurn nodes ingested into Neo4j

decision: Use Serper API (not Tavily) for competitive intelligence gathering

decision: Propagate upstream cell context to downstream cells via synthesis + conversation summary in topological order

decision: Add /investments route showing all projects and member completion state for syndicate members

decision: Capture investor views through conversation in cell deep-dives instead of form responses

decision: Use JavaScript DOM reordering to move SVG connector paths behind box elements on page load

decision: Implement hover-dim via CSS opacity transition with 0.18s duration and 10% target opacity for non-hovered elements
reason: Smooth fade provides visual feedback without jarring flicker; 10% opacity keeps context visible while clearly highlighting the focused box

decision: Render SVG connector paths behind all box groups via JavaScript DOM reorder on page load
reason: Lines were covering text; moving paths to the bottom of the SVG stack ensures text remains readable and visible

decision: Implement geometry-based hover highlight that detects connected boxes by checking if path endpoints land near a hovered box
reason: Users need to see not just the hovered box but the entire connected subgraph; geometry-based detection is more reliable than attribute-based lookup when SVG structure is complex

decision: Deploy lld-diagram.html to GitHub Pages and auto-update on every push via gh API
reason: Provides a clean, shareable URL (https://lochan4.github.io/lld-diagram/) that requires no login; every file push automatically redeploys the latest version

decision: Render SVG connector paths behind box elements via JavaScript DOM reordering on page load
reason: SVG paints elements in document order; moving paths to the end of the SVG stack ensures they render underneath all boxes without modifying the HTML structure

decision: Implement smart hover highlighting using geometric endpoint detection to identify connected boxes and paths
reason: Investors need to see the full context of a box's relationships; highlighting only the hovered box is insufficient; endpoint detection is more reliable than string matching on IDs

decision: Use CSS clip-path to constrain text overflow within box boundaries
reason: Long text lines that overflow into adjacent boxes create visual confusion and reduce readability; clip-path provides clean, performant clipping without modifying text content

decision: Implement CSS clip-path on all SVG box groups to prevent text overflow and maintain visual hierarchy in lld-diagram.html
